steps: Uncrate & fit a base kit
Remove the crate, cover and pallet lag bolts (7/16" / 12mm socket), lay the unit on its back and bolt on a base kit — short base, legs, pedestal or wood box. One is required.

Remove the crate top and supports, then the plastic cover. With a 7/16" (12mm) wrench/socket, remove the lag bolts holding the hold-down brackets and the unit to the pallet, lay the unit on its back and take off the brackets.

Base kit — one is required

  • Short base — masonry hearth only (see Floor protection). Carriage bolts go up through the square holes in the base and the side edges of the firebox bottom; secure with nuts and washers.
  • Legs — four 1/4-20 x 1" carriage bolts up through the square holes in the side edges of the firebox bottom; nuts and washers.
  • Pedestal — carriage bolts up through the pedestal side flanges and the firebox bottom edges; nuts and washers.
  • Wood box — bolt on as for the legs. The wood box back must be installed for stability (screws loose in the back edge of the legs, drop the back on, tighten). Levelling legs screw into the nutserts; the bottom panel is optional (pem studs, washers and nuts, two each side).

Decals: leg and wood box builds get the French "Do Not Overfire" label (Part #500000354) and the PE Bubble sticker (Part #5039) from the instruction pack. Short base and pedestal come with the English label and sticker already attached.

Note: the rating label (p. 3) gives the short base kit number as #11130030; the parts list (p. 39) gives it as 11130027.
Hang the side panels
Guide each panel's front tabs into the bracket (and leg) slots and push back; screw the rear to the rear-shield bracket with a fibre washer under each screw head to protect the enamel.
Floor protection

Short base: masonry hearth raised 11" (280mm) min. Other bases on a combustible floor need continuous non-combustible ember protection — USA 16" front and 8" to the sides of the door opening; Canada 18" firing side, 8" other sides.
Clearances & position
Set the stove to the clearances (single-wall: 14" side, 13" back, 11" corner; double-wall: 10", 6", 8"). Alcove: max. depth 36", min. height 7', min. width 47".
Chimney & connector
6" listed (ULC-S629 / UL-103HT) or lined masonry chimney, 15 feet min. system height, never shared. Plumb-bob the ceiling and roof holes; crimped connector end into the collar with three screws.

1. Position the floor protection and stove to the clearances diagram.
  2. Hang a string and plumb-bob over the exact center of the stove's flue pipe to mark the ceiling and roof holes.
  3. Check for floor joists, ceiling joists and rafters; adjust if needed and reconfirm clearances.
  4. Install the listed chimney from the ceiling through to the rain cap per its maker's directions.
  5. Slip the connector's crimped edge inside the stove collar and secure it with three screws through the collar holes.
  6. Add the remaining lengths up to the finished chimney height, secured to each other, using the manufacturer's approved adapter; a slip section helps.

Single-wall connector: 6" diameter, 24 gauge black pipe, clean and new, as short and straight as possible, crimped (male) ends down, 3 sheet metal screws at every joint and collar. Offsets: every connector, offset elbow and chimney joint takes at least three sheet metal screws, with the chimney maker's listed offset support. Masonry chimneys must be cleaned and inspected by a professional for cracks, weak mortar or deterioration.
Combustion air
Room air through the airbox bottom, or outside air via 4" metal duct and adapter (SKU #11100005) — required in mobile homes. A residential stove on outside air must be secured to the structure.
Mobile home requirements
Two 1/4" x 2" or longer lag screws to the floor, outside air, a listed double-wall connector (no horizontal connector) and a ULC-S629 / UL-103HT chimney; never in a sleeping room.

• Do not install in a sleeping room; do not connect to a chimney flue serving another appliance.
  • Maintain the structural integrity of the mobile home floor, wall and ceiling/roof.
  • Attach the stove to the floor with two 1/4" x 2" or longer lag screws: through the leg anchors (leg model), the pedestal base (pedestal model) or the holes in the bottom sides of the wood box (wood box model).
  • Outside combustion air must be used (outside air kit).
  • Listed double-wall connector and a compatible ULC-S629 or UL-103HT listed chimney; horizontal connector not permitted.

Clearances are the double-wall values (Figure 23).
Firebrick
Lay the bricks to Figure 24 — rear wall, then side walls, then floor. The fire burns directly on them; replace any broken or missing bricks.

A9" X 4 1/2" X 1 1/4" (230 mm x 115 mm x 32 mm)
B2" X 9" X 1 1/4" (51 mm x 230 mm x 32 mm)
D2" X 4 7/16" X 1 1/4" (51mm x 113 mm x 32 mm)
E4 7/16" X 3 1/4" X 1 1/4 (113 mm x 83 mm x 32 mm)
  1. Rear wall: two A bricks standing behind the right tab on the brick rail, slid toward center; on the left, two A with one B between them, slid toward center.
  2. Each side wall: E up into the back corner, then an A underneath while holding the E; B up under the baffle tube box, then two A while holding the B.
  3. Floor: an A in each corner and one B (Figure 29, back row); two A in front of the left rear A, slid back to touch; two A on the right, then a D in the center in front of the B.

The layout is shown as Figure 24. Firebrick set: 80002938.
Free the flue gas agitator
Take the thermocouple guard out of the flue collar, remove the cardboard holding the flue gas agitator, check its rear pin, then refit the guard with all three ends seated.

1. Remove the thermocouple guard from inside the flue collar.
  2. Remove the piece of cardboard holding the flue gas agitator in place, and verify the agitator's rear pin is in place.
  3. Re-install the thermocouple guard with all three ends in place correctly.
Do not operate with the flue gas agitator removed.
Connect power
Plug the A/C adapter's barrel plug into the control board and the adapter into a wall outlet; add the optional battery box if used. Keep cords out from under the heater.

Take the A/C adapter (Wall Adapter 12V, 80002838) from inside the unit, connect its barrel plug to the A/C adapter plug in the control board, then plug the adapter into a wall outlet. Do not route the power cord beneath the heater.

After any unplugging, wait a minimum of 30 seconds before plugging back in. A power flicker can freeze the control board; reset it by unplugging the adapter for at least 30 seconds.

Optional battery box: follow the instructions included with it. It sits low on the right side panel, held by magnets; batteries last an estimated 5-7 days under continuous use. With it the appliance is fully functional in a power failure; without it, the unit still operates within safe and certified limits on the manual air control.

items: Wood too wet → use dry wood
Air turned down too soon → wait for a good bed of coals and charred wood
Draft too low → chimney plugged or restricted, improper chimney height and/or diameter; provide outside air, check draft
Glass only: door gasket leakage → replace gasket, check door latch

items: Wood may be wet → use drier wood
Fire too small → build a larger fire; open the draft control
Draft too low → chimney plugged or restricted; inspect and clean

items: Air control set too high → set it lower
Not enough wood → unsplit wood is preferred for overnight burns
Draft too high → excessive chimney height and/or diameter (Figure 17 / 18)

items: Combustion air supply blocked → check the outside air supply for obstructions
Check that the room air cover is removed

light.title: Lighting a fire
light.html:
Never use chemicals or any other volatile liquid to start a fire. Fire starters made from paper, cardboard, sawdust or wax are fine.

  1. Move the air control to High — all the way to the left — and open the door.
  2. Put crumpled newspaper in the center of the stove. Crisscross several pieces of small, dry kindling over it, then add a few pieces of larger kindling on top.
  3. Light the paper. Leave the door open about 1/2" (13 mm) to 1" (25 mm) until the kindling is fully in flames. Never leave the stove unattended with the door open.
  4. Once the kindling is fully engulfed, add a few small pieces of wood and close the door.
  5. When there's a good bed of coals and the wood has charred, switch to normal operation with the air control.

Restarting from overnight coals

Open the door and rake the hot embers toward the front. Add a couple of dry, split logs on top and close the door. Set the air to High; the logs should start burning within a few minutes. Once they've charred, set the air where you want it.

Your first 2-3 fires bake on the paint. Open all windows and doors, since the smoke and fumes can bother some people, and follow the Stove Bright (Forrest Paint) sheet that came with the stove. Smoke detectors may go off more often. Don't disconnect them.

air.title: Using the air control
air.html:
The air control sits beneath the door. Facing the stove, it runs from Low on the right to High on the left, and the middle counts as medium. Any position in between sets the burn rate and heat you want. Practice will show you what suits your wood, chimney and weather.

High

Use High to light the fire and to char fresh wood after reloading, for about 10–15 minutes or until the wood is fully charred. Drier wood chars faster. Don't run on High for long periods, or you risk over-firing the stove.

Low

Low is for overnight or extended burns, and unsplit logs work best. Char the wood completely on the highest setting first, then turn the air down slowly.

Reloading

Move the air to High and give the fire time to brighten. Then open the door slowly so smoke doesn't puff out. Load wood parallel to the stove front with room for air between the logs, and never so high that opening the door gets hazardous.

Have the optional blower? When the air control is on Low, run the blower on Low too, or the fire may go out.
The minimum low burn rate is set at the factory. Altering it is against federal regulations.

wood.title: Choosing and testing wood
wood.html:
Burn natural wood only. Air-dried, seasoned hardwood burns more efficiently and cleanly than softwood or freshly cut wood, and the denser the dry wood, the more heat it gives.

Ideal length17 inches
Maximum length18 inches
Drying timesix months or more

Store wood under cover, away from open flame or heat. Wet wood smoulders, makes lots of smoke and creosote, gives little heat and tends to go out. It can cut heat output by up to 25%. Never try an overnight burn with green or wet wood.

Test a piece

Put a large piece on a good bed of coals. Burning on more than one side within one minute: it's dry. Turns black and lights within three minutes: it's damp. Sizzles, hisses and blackens without lighting in five minutes: it's too wet to burn.

Never burn

Wet or green wood, unseasoned wood, treated wood, salt water wood, garbage, coal or charcoal, lawn clippings or yard waste, railroad ties, solvents, waste petroleum products, paints, paint thinners or asphalt products, construction or demolition debris, paper products, cardboard, plywood or particleboard, manure or animal remains, and anything containing rubber (including tires), plastic or asbestos. Burning these materials may release toxic fumes or make the stove ineffective and cause smoke. Salt water wood and garbage contain chlorides that rapidly destroy metal and void the warranty. Charcoal can produce deadly carbon monoxide, so never barbecue in the stove.

Note: on wet wood, the manual's do-not-burn list (p. 26) includes wet or green wood and unseasoned wood, and p. 5 says not to burn wet wood; but p. 28 says that if you feel it is necessary to burn wet or unseasoned wood, do so only with the air control set open enough to maintain a good strong fire and fairly high chimney temperatures, and not to attempt to burn overnight using green wood or wet wood.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the glass with fireplace glass cleaner, and only when the stove is cold.

  • Don't use abrasive cleaners.
  • Never scrape with anything that might scratch the glass.
  • Don't clean it while it's hot.

What the deposit tells you

A light brown, dusty film that wipes off easily usually means good burning and dry, seasoned wood, so your pipes and chimney are fairly clean. A black, greasy deposit that's hard to remove comes from wet or green wood and burning too slowly. That buildup is forming at least as fast in your chimney.

Protect the glass

Don't slam the door, and make sure no logs stick out where they'd hit the glass as it closes. If the glass cracks or breaks, replace it before you use the stove again, with ceramic glass only (22 3/4" x 16-1/8" x 5 mm) from your dealer.

Glass that keeps getting dirty can also mean the door gasket is leaking. The fix is a new gasket and a check of the door latch.

ash.title: Removing ashes
ash.html:
Remove ashes only when the fire has burned down and the stove is cold.

  • Take out the excess once ashes are 3" (76 mm) to 4" (102 mm) deep.
  • Always leave a bed about 1" (25 mm) deep. It helps keep a hot charcoal bed.
  • Keep the front of the firebox, where extra combustion air comes in, clear of heavy ash so the air can flow.

The stove has no ash shelf, so take care when you open the door and load wood.

Disposing of ashes

Put ashes in a metal container with a tight-fitting lid. Set the closed container on a non-combustible floor or on the ground, well away from anything that can burn. If you'll bury or scatter the ashes, keep them in the closed container until every cinder has cooled completely. Don't put other waste in the same container.

chimney.title: Creosote and chimney fires
chimney.html:
Slow, smoky fires leave creosote, a tar-like deposit, in the chimney. If it ignites, it makes an extremely hot fire, and temperatures inside the chimney can exceed 2000°F (1100°C).

  • Have the connector and chimney inspected at least once every two months in the heating season. Remove creosote once it's 3 mm or more thick.
  • Until you know your stove, check for creosote daily. Weekly cleaning may be needed in mild weather; monthly is usually enough in the coldest months.
  • Burn clean: dry wood, small loads of two or three logs, and the air fairly wide open for the first 10 to 30 minutes after loading.

Signs of a chimney fire

Flames and sparks shooting out the top, a roaring sound, or a vibrating chimney.

If it happens

  1. Get everyone ready to leave, with a meeting place outside.
  2. Close the air control on the stove.
  3. Call the fire department, and keep a fire extinguisher handy.
  4. Before the next fire, have the chimney cleaned and checked for stress and cracks. Check combustibles around the chimney and the roof too.

safety.title: Safety around the stove
safety.html:
• The stove is hot while it runs. Keep children, clothing and furniture away. Hot glass will burn, so never let children touch it.
  • Keep the loading door closed while burning, and open it only to add wood.
  • Never use gasoline, lantern fuel, kerosene, charcoal lighter fluid or similar liquids to start or "freshen up" a fire. Keep them well away.
  • Burn right on the firebricks, never on a grate or andirons. Replace broken or missing bricks.
  • Keep wood and other combustibles out of the clearance space. With the wood box base, only wood goes underneath, at least 1" (25 mm) below the bottom of the airbox.
  • Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors are strongly recommended near the stove. Don't disconnect them.

Signs it's running too hot

Pushing the stove past what it's designed for can permanently damage it and the chimney. A top or vent pipe glowing red means you're over-firing. Leaving that uncorrected can be hazardous and may void the warranty. An uncontrollable burn, or a stove part or chimney glowing red, signals too much draft. Smoke leaking into the room at the stove or pipe joints signals too little.

care.title: Routine checks and maintenance
care.html:
Look for cracks, heavy corrosion, burned-out sections and excessive warping. If you find damage, contact your dealer. Running the stove with broken parts can damage other parts and may void the warranty.

WeeklyFirebrick for cracks; door gasket for sagging, placement, damage
MonthlyBaffle tubes, brick rails and tabs, baffle air tube, back of the airwash chamber, baffle locking pin, boost tube cover holes
Every six monthsVacuum the optional blower's grill openings

Baffle

Some warping, up to 1/4" or 6.5mm, is normal. Replace the baffle if it's permanently warped more than that, or cracked or broken. Never run the stove with the baffle, tubes or insulation removed.

Door gasket

The 1" (25 mm) fiberglass rope gasket needs only light pressure to seal. Keep it in good condition and replace it when needed with the kit from your dealer. The door catch can be adjusted to change the pressure on the gasket.

Use only materials supplied by the manufacturer for maintenance and replacements.

power.title: Power and batteries
power.html:
The stove's control board runs on an A/C adapter plugged into a wall outlet. Keep the cord out from under the stove.

If the controls freeze

A flicker in the power can freeze the control board. Unplug the adapter from the wall, wait at least 30 seconds, and plug it back in. Any time you unplug the stove, wait the same 30 seconds before plugging it in again.

Power outages

  • With the optional battery box, the stove stays fully functional. Batteries last an estimated 5-7 days of continuous use.
  • Without it, the stove still runs within safe, certified limits on the manual air control at the front.

Changing the batteries

  1. The battery box sits low on the right side panel as you face the stove, held on by magnets. Lift it off so the cover faces up, without pulling on its wires.
  2. Release the catch at the end and lift off the cover.
  3. Replace the old batteries with new ones.
  4. Put the cover back and return the box to the side panel.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Pacific Energy covers the original registered purchaser:

Limited lifetime (10 years)Parts only: porcelain finish, glass (thermal breakage only, not impact), plating, firebox, baffle
3 year comprehensiveParts and labor on any defective part, including blowers, speed controls and thermal switches

Not covered

  • Firebrick, gaskets and ceramic fiber blankets. Firebox rails and heat shields aren't in the lifetime coverage.
  • Labor under the lifetime coverage.
  • Misuse, abuse, improper installation, accident, lack of maintenance or modification.

Early wear usually points to improper use, such as too much draft, heating too large an area, or contaminated fuel, and may void coverage. Tampering with the air control assembly, or burning salt water wood or garbage, voids it; uncorrected over-firing may too.

Making a claim

Contact your Pacific Energy dealer with proof of purchase, the purchase date, and the model name and serial number. Register online at pacificenergy.net/register. The serial number is on the certification label or the manual cover.

This is a summary. The full terms are in the official PDF.

specOutput.title: Heat output, efficiency and emissions
specOutput.html:
EPA BTU output13,240 to 29,536 Btu/hr
Maker's website: EPA Test Fuel 29,500 BTU.
HHV tested efficiency73%
LHV tested efficiency79%
EPA certified emissions1.6 grams per hour
CO emissions1.6 grams per minute
FuelSeasoned cord wood

Meets the EPA 2020 cribwood particulate limits for wood heaters sold after May 15, 2020; tested to EPA Method 28R. Efficiencies are weighted averages per CSA B415. The output range uses burn rates from the low and high EPA tests with Douglas Fir dimensional lumber. CO varies with fuel and how the unit is operated.

specWood.title: Wood length and fuel
specWood.html:
Ideal wood length17 inches
Maximum wood length18 inches

Solid fuel (cordwood) only. Load parallel to the stove front, logs up to 18"(460 mm). No grate or andirons: build the fire directly on the firebrick. Wet wood can cause up to a 25% drop in heater output.

specFlue.title: Flue, chimney and connector
specFlue.html:
Flue size (stove outlet)6 inches
Minimum system height15 feet (4.6 m.) from base of appliance
Chimney exit3 feet (1 m.) above roof; two feet (0.6 m.) above highest projection within 10 feet (3 m.)
Connector6 inch / 150MM min. 24 MSG black, or listed
Single-wall connector to combustibles18 inches / 455mm

Chimney: ULC-S629 or UL-103HT listed stainless, or a lined masonry chimney suitable for solid fuel, in good condition. Listings: Canada ULC S-641 double-wall connector and ULC-S629 chimney; USA UL-103 HT connector and chimney. Never share a flue with another appliance; changing the flue size may adversely affect performance.

The connector must not pass through an attic, roof space, closet, concealed space, floor or ceiling. Wall pass-throughs follow CAN/CSA-B365 or NFPA 211; the manual's Systems A–D need a minimum of 12 in. (305mm), 9 in. (229mm), 6 in. (152mm) and 2 in. (51mm) to combustibles. Figure 17 calls for a 12" (305mm) minimum first section of pipe: the unit may be harder to start, so give it as much vertical length as possible. Dimensions for each base are drawings on pp. 6–7.

specClear.html:
Residential installation with a single-wall connector, from the rating label:

specFloor.title: Floor protection and hearth
specFloor.html:
Leg, pedestal and wood box builds may go on a combustible floor with non-combustible ember protection. The short base must sit on a masonry hearth (concrete, concrete block, brick or stone, or steel stud construction with a minimum 1" thick top of those materials and non-combustible board for all other sides) raised a minimum of 11"(280mm) above the floor; ember protection is still required.

USA16" (405 mm) front; 8" (205 mm) to the sides of the fuel loading door opening
USA min. size34 5/8"(880mm) wide × 37 3/8"(949mm) overall depth
Canada18" (460 mm) firing side; 8" (205 mm) other sides
Canada min. size43 1/4"(1.1m) wide × 47 3/4"(1.21m) overall depth
Horizontal connectorprotection under it, plus 2" (55 mm) beyond each side

The floor protector drawings also note "Type 1 floor protector - approved to UL1618, Minimum 20GA steel". Don't obstruct the space beneath the heater.

Note: for US floor protection, p. 13 gives 16" (405 mm) to the front and 8" (205 mm) to the sides of the fuel loading door opening; the rating label drawing on p. 3 lists US values of 16 inches / 410 mm (G), 5 inches / 130 mm (H) and 0 inches (I).

specAir.title: Combustion air
specAir.html:
Outside air is necessary for mobile home installations and optional for residential. Otherwise the stove draws room air through the opening in the airbox bottom.

  • Through the floor: a hole large enough for 4" diameter metal duct behind the unit, drawing from a ventilated crawl space or ducted to the outdoors. Attach the 4" outside air adapter to the airbox bottom and connect with 4"(100mm) i.d. metal duct.
  • Through the wall behind: a 4"(100mm) air intake; fit the 4" outside air adapter (SKU #11100005) over the hole in the airbox bottom and run metal duct to the intake.

A residential stove on outside air must be secured to the structure so the duct can't dislodge. Figure 17: 4" (100 mm) diameter air inlet with rodent screen, hooded vent or 90° elbow turned down; a well-ventilated crawl space needn't be extended outside. The intake location on the stove is shown as a drawing on p. 17.

specBlower.title: Optional blower
specBlower.html:
Blower kitpart # 11140001
Electrical rating115 volts AC-1.02 amps
Fan output rating160 CFM

Three-prong power cord; install any time per the kit's instructions and route the cord away from the heater. "Auto" on the fan-housing rocker switch starts the fan as the stove heats and stops it once cooled; "Man" bypasses the temperature sensing device and runs until switched off. Run it on Low when the air control is on "L" or the unit may go out. Vacuum the grill openings at least every six months.

Note: the rating label (p. 3) gives the blower's electrical rating as 115V, 60HZ, 1.0 AMP; p. 23 gives 115 volts AC-1.02 amps.

Blower electrical rating: rating label gives 115V, 60HZ, 1.0 AMP; Optional Blower section gives 115 volts AC-1.02 amps.

US ember protection: p. 13 text gives 16" (405 mm) front and 8" (205 mm) to the sides of the fuel loading door opening; rating label drawing gives US G 16 inches / 410 mm, H 5 inches / 130 mm, I 0 inches. G/H/I are keyed only by the drawing (positions suggest front / side / back), so whether H is measured from the stove body or the door opening can't be confirmed from text. Canada values agree (18/8/8).

Each figure value is exactly 3 in. more than a label value (consistent with measuring to the 6 in. flue centerline), but the reference points are only drawn. Unit clearances 14/13/11 agree.
Double-wall connector clearances: label D/E/F = 20 5/8 / 9 1/4 / 17 1/2 in.; Figures 16 and 23 show 23 5/8, 12 1/4 and 20 1/2 in. (again each 3 in. more). Unit clearances 10/6/8 agree.

The DO NOT BURN list (p. 26) includes "Wet or green wood" and "Unseasoned wood", and To Avoid a Chimney Fire (p. 5) says "Do not burn wet wood or turn down the unit too quickly after loading"; p. 28 says "If you feel it is necessary to burn wet or unseasoned wood, do so only with the air inlet set open enough to maintain a good strong fire and fairly high chimney temperatures. Do not attempt to burn overnight using green wood or wet wood." Both shown in an amber note in the wood drawer.

review.notes: p. 3 efficiency box: the layout text lists 73% / 79% out of order relative to the LHV/HHV labels; the raw text extract of the same page pairs LHV Tested Efficiency 79% and HHV Tested Efficiency 73% (matches catalog 73% HHV). Rating label clearance letters A-F are defined in the label text; the single-wall vs double-wall value groups were confirmed by the asterisked 16 1/4 in. (as-tested note tied to the single-wall heading) and by Figure 16 unit clearances (14/13/11 single wall, 10/6/8 double wall). French label text gives the leg kit as no 11130024; English label and parts list give 11130029 (guide doesn't cite a leg kit number). Not transcribed (drawings only, fractions garbled): stove dimensions for each base (pp. 6-7), outside air intake location (p. 17), Figure 17/18 dimensions other than the labelled 12 in. minimum first section and 4 in. inlet. The 'Type 1 floor protector - approved to UL1618, Minimum 20GA steel' note appears on the p. 3 and p. 13 drawings; which country's drawing it belongs to isn't clear from the text, so it is quoted without assigning it. p. 3 states 'CO emissions are 1.6 grams per minute' (quoted as printed). The manual mentions a control board, flue and firebox thermocouples, motor control assembly and a 12V wall adapter but never explains what the electronics do in normal operation; the guide covers only what is stated (adapter hookup, 30-second reset, battery box, power-failure behavior). Battery type/count for the optional battery box isn't given. Mobile home floor anchoring lists leg, pedestal and wood box models only; the short base isn't mentioned there. Not in the manual, so left out: firebox volume, weight, burn times, heating area, cordwood max output (catalog 85,000), non-catalytic/Extended Burn Technology wording, stainless components. p. 31 says 'See Replacement Parts List page 38', but the parts list is on p. 39 (p. 38 is troubleshooting). Pages 42-43 are blank. No French-only or scrambled text needed decoding.
